$comment: The site's pack map, declared. A map that says zero is a decision, and a page
with no map is a drift; this is the file the check and the test both read, so
there is one expectation and two independent readers of it: this repository's
DOM (a test that renders the real composition) and this repository's built
export (the script below, which reads the emitted HTML and the emitted CSS).
The rule being enforced, in one sentence: a pack boundary lands on a mark and
nowhere else, and exactly three regions of a page may carry a pack that is not
the page's own ground.
The third region is the hero. The header switcher and the products band were
already two, and both are one row of marks beside something else. The hero's
right column is a third such row, and it is the reason this page is allowed to
have any colour on it at all: a boundary may only land on a ProductMark, so a
mark is the one element that can wear a hue other than the ground's, and eleven
marks across three rows is every hue this design system will let a consumer put
on one page. The law is not a limit to work around. It is the reason the page's
colour is four identifiable pastels and a spectrum rather than a gradient.
`peach` appears nowhere in this file. Four products own four pastels, this site
owns the ground, and Prism owns none because prism.nanisoft.com renders with no
data-pack at all, so the fifth pastel is still unowned and the architecture
caption's claim that peach is reserved for what the factory builds next is what
makes that caption true rather than a hope.
`regions` lists every region that carries a boundary at all, with the exact
multiset of packs each one carries, so a boundary added by accident is a finding
in both readers. `secondPackRegions` is the rule restated, and it is asserted as
well as derived: a page that grows a fourth region carrying a second pack fails
the build.

header.switcher.why: The company site is the apex, so its switcher is the whole product set, and a set that tells five products apart is the reason four packs and a spectrum are on one page at all. Four members carry a pack that is not the ground; the fifth is this site, whose own mark is the pack the page is painted in; and Prism carries none, because prism.nanisoft.com renders with no data-pack at all and a mark with no pack is drawn as the spectrum rather than as a colourless dot.

header.brand.why: The header's brand lockup is this site, and this site's pack is the page's pack, so its boundary is the ground rather than a second pack.

footer.brand.why: The same lockup, in the footer. A ground is stable for the life of a page, and a footer that wore a different hue from the page it closes would be a second claim about the same thing.

landing.hero.why: The hero's identity column is the whole product set at the largest size a mark is drawn at, one mark per member. It is the one claim on this page a reader can check rather than take: four products in four pastels, this site in the ground, and the design system in the spectrum it is. Every boundary is a ProductMark, which is a fully rounded disc, so the boundary moves nothing about any shape.

landing.products.why: A product row's mark is that product's own hue, and it is the one claim in this section a reader makes a decision from: which product is this, and does its colour mean anything. The mark is a fully rounded disc, so the boundary moves nothing about its shape. The region is named by the Block that draws it rather than by an ordinal the band used to print, so deleting the section numbers cannot rename a pack region.
